rows.subtype: Living with a very direct sibling [Receiver]
rows.description: A sibling on the receiving end of blunt remarks feels criticised even when no harm is meant. Tells the other how the words land, and separates the honest content from the tone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult assumes good intent, lends money and helps without limit. Generosity is a strength, but they may need practice spotting when kindness is being used and setting limits.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A wise person practises warm assertiveness: agreeing where it is true and declining where it is not. Says no without a long apology and accepts that some disappointment is not the same as cruelty.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A team sees someone always supportive who rarely asks for credit or raises. Their goodwill glues the group together, yet they are easy to overload; fair leaders share the load and the recognition.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A toddler cries hard at loud noises, separation or a changed routine and takes a long time to settle. This is sensitivity of the nervous system, not bad parenting or bad behaviour, and steady comfort helps.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child keeps asking what if questions about monsters, storms or a parent being late. Worry feels real and big; calm answers and predictable routines soothe more than being told there is nothing to fear.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, anxiety, calm

rows.description: A child gets stomach aches before tests and replays small embarrassments for days. Feels emotions strongly and slowly recovers, and benefits from naming feelings and practising small steps.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager swings between worry, irritation and low confidence over grades, looks and friends. Puberty amplifies emotion; the pattern is common, and it becomes a concern when it stops daily life.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, anxiety, doubt

rows.description: A classmate sees a friend who overthinks messages and cancels plans at the last moment. It is not drama; being patient, steady and consistent makes the friend feel less alone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A wise approach treats big feelings as signals to slow down, not as proof of danger. Sleep, movement, naming worry and sharing with someone trusted help, and persistent distress deserves a professional conversation.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, anxiety, trust
